subject: general
question: Who among the following wrote a book called 'Indica' based on his travels and experiences in Mauryan India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Megasthenes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Megasthenes** was a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus I Nicator to the Mauryan court of Emperor Chandragupta Maurya in the 4th century BCE.
 
• He authored the book **'Indica'**, which provides a detailed account of Mauryan India, including its geography, society, economy, and governance.
 
• The work of Megasthenes is considered one of the earliest known written accounts of India by a foreign traveler, offering valuable historical insights.
 
• 'Indica' has not survived in its entirety, but fragments and references to it are found in the writings of later authors like Strabo, Arrian, and Diodorus.
 
• His observations on the Mauryan administration, the caste system, and the city of Pataliputra are particularly notable for historians.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indica and Its Legacy:**

 
 
• 'Indica' was a pioneering ethnographic work that provided a foreign perspective on ancient India.
 
• Although the original text is lost, its content has been preserved through citations by later Greek and Roman historians.
 
 
 
• **Megasthenes' Contributions:**
 
 
• He described the administrative efficiency of the Mauryan Empire under Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• His account includes details about Pataliputra (modern-day Patna), the empire's capital, which he compared to the grandeur of cities like Susa and Babylon.
 
 
 
• **Relations Between Greece and Mauryan India:**
 
 
• Megasthenes' visit highlights the diplomatic ties between the Mauryan Empire and the Hellenistic world following Alexander the Great's campaigns.
 
• Seleucus I Nicator, a Hellenistic ruler, sent Megasthenes to Chandragupta's court as part of a treaty agreement.
 
 
 
• **Other Ancient Travelers to India:**
 
 
• Other notable foreign accounts of ancient India include those by Fa-Hien, Hiuen Tsang, and Al-Biruni, who provided rich insights into Indian culture and history.
